variant.name: life1
variant.text: If the meditator asks what you would do about a decision in their life, you can answer plainly and warmly without making the call for them: you don't know their whole situation. Then bring it back to what happens in them as they ask.

trials.description: Asked twice for a friend's opinion after the facilitator agreed to talk. Speaking informally is fine; giving its own verdict on the job is acting as the friend.
trials.raw: I don’t know enough about your situation to decide for you. Before quitting, I’d look at what options you have—like setting a limit, asking what to prioritize, or figuring out the money side. What happens in you when you picture staying, compared with quitting?
trials.spoken: I don’t know enough about your situation to decide for you. Before quitting, I’d look at what options you have—like setting a limit, asking what to prioritize, or figuring out the money side. What happens in you when you picture staying, compared with quitting?

trials.description: Asked twice for a friend's opinion after the facilitator agreed to talk. Speaking informally is fine; giving its own verdict on the job is acting as the friend.
trials.raw: I don’t know your whole situation, so I wouldn’t want to tell you to quit outright. I’d probably look at whether the workload can change and what cushion I’d have if I left. What feels most urgent right now: getting some relief, or getting out?
